rows.title: Re-importing a jobs file whose entries have ids but no numeric updatedAt adds one more duplicate of every job touched since, on every import
rows.summary: Now: re-importing the same file after editing a job adds the file's version once as a copy (nothing dropped); every later import of that file skips it, because mergeImport also compares a timeless entry with the copies already in the list (src/utils/jobMerge.js). Review: to-dos' and interviews' ids the import makes up are taken from the job here when comparing, so id-less interviews no longer defeat the match.

issues: 9d05d4d0 fixes the root cause it names: the id finds only the edited original, so it now also compares a timeless entry with the other jobs here (asOver takes their times and to-do ids). Its failfirst (run 36651752745) is real: 2 of 3 tests fail without the fix; the third guards that a different row is still added as a copy. It changes nothing for entries with a numeric updatedAt, the untouched-demo case or entries whose id is new; the store's importJobs is its only caller; the sync, undo and exports do not go through it.

Gap, fixed in bc5420aa: completeJob gives an interview with no id a new id on every import, and asOver took only the to-dos' ids from the job here. So a timeless file whose jobs had id-less interviews added one more copy of each such job on EVERY import, even with nothing edited here (the fix's own new check never matched either). asOver now takes the interviews' ids from the job here the same way (idsFrom). Test: tests/unit/r5-hunt10-job-import-interviews.unit.mjs, 2 of 3 fail without the fix.
review.notes: Run 36653059545 on bc5420aa: failfirst green ('# fail 2' without the fix, pass with it); 79/79 job import, store, normalize and knowledge-docs tests pass; lint passes. Left as is, low: if the user deletes the edited original and keeps the copy an earlier import added, the next import adds the file's job back under its own id next to the identical copy. That happens once only, because the one after skips it by id. The new check applies only when the entry's id is here, which keeps the file's own same-id duplicates matching as before. No accessibility issues noted.

notes: CI run 36651752745 (failfirst + job import/store/knowledge-docs tests) was still running when this report was written; lint passed.
